verses.english: Linked Discourses 22.5
1. Nakula’s Father
Development of Immersion
So I have heard.
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, develop immersion.
A mendicant who has immersion truly understands.
What do they truly understand?

verses.pali: Rūpassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca, vedanāya samudayañca atthaṅgamañca, saññāya samudayañca atthaṅgamañca, saṅkhārānaṁ samudayañca atthaṅgamañca, viññāṇassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca.
verses.english: The origin and ending of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.

verses.pali: Ko ca, bhikkhave, rūpassa samudayo, ko vedanāya samudayo, ko saññāya samudayo, ko saṅkhārānaṁ samudayo, ko viññāṇassa samudayo?
verses.english: And what is the origin of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu abhinandati abhivadati ajjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant approves, welcomes, and keeps clinging.
What do they approve, welcome, and keep clinging to?
They approve, welcome, and keep clinging to form.

verses.pali: Tassa rūpaṁ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato uppajjati nandī.
verses.english: This gives rise to relishing.
Relishing forms is grasping.
Their grasping is a requirement for continued existence.
Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.
Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress to come to be.
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
They approve, welcome, and keep clinging to feeling …
perception …
choices …
consciousness.

verses.pali: Tassa viññāṇaṁ abhinandato abhivadato ajjhosāya tiṭṭhato uppajjati nandī.
verses.english: This gives rise to relishing.
Relishing consciousness is grasping.
Their grasping is a requirement for continued existence.
Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth.
Rebirth is a condition that gives rise to old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress.
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
This is the origin of form,
feeling,
perception,
choices,
and consciousness.

verses.pali: Ko ca, bhikkhave, rūpassa atthaṅgamo, ko vedanāya …
verses.english: And what is the ending of form, feeling,
perception,
choices,
and consciousness?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, nābhinandati nābhivadati nājjhosāya tiṭṭhati.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant doesn’t approve, welcome, or keep clinging.
What don’t they approve, welcome, or keep clinging to?
They don’t approve, welcome, or keep clinging to form.

verses.pali: Tassa rūpaṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato yā rūpe nandī sā nirujjhati.
verses.english: As a result, relishing of form ceases.
When that relishing ceases, grasping ceases.
When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.
They don’t approve, welcome, or keep clinging to feeling …

verses.pali: Tassa vedanaṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato yā vedanāya nandī sā nirujjhati.

verses.english: perception …
choices …

verses.pali: Tassa saṅkhāre anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato yā saṅkhāresu nandī sā nirujjhati.

verses.english: consciousness.

verses.pali: Tassa viññāṇaṁ anabhinandato anabhivadato anajjhosāya tiṭṭhato yā viññāṇe nandī sā nirujjhati.
verses.english: As a result, relishing of consciousness ceases.
When that relishing ceases, grasping ceases. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, rūpassa atthaṅgamo, ayaṁ vedanāya atthaṅgamo, ayaṁ saññāya atthaṅgamo, ayaṁ saṅkhārānaṁ atthaṅgamo, ayaṁ viññāṇassa atthaṅgamo”ti.
verses.english: This is the ending of form, feeling, perception, choices, and consciousness.”
